interest: Shows 1945 Allied tracking of Japanese capital flight and Takasaki's account of Manchuria's industrial collapse under looting and Soviet removals.
overview: File 894.503100 (1945) covers Japanese overseas capital: cross-reference sheets on Japanese funds moved from German to neutral banks and Latin American expropriation decrees, plus a note on Tatsunosuke Takasaki's finding that Manchuria's industrial capital was nearly wiped out by looting and Soviet dismantling.

people.name: Tatsunosuke Takasaki
people.role: Former President of the Manchuria Heavy Industry Development Co.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a report forwarded by the Treasury Department and FEA concerning Japanese residents transferring funds from German banks to neutral European nations.
subfiles.summary: Indexes a March 1945 Bern telegram reporting Japanese nationals in Germany moved their bank funds to neutral European countries.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Bern Telegram No. 1044 on Japanese Capital Flight from Germany

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a circular telegram regarding expropriation decrees over commercial and financial entities representing German or Japanese interests in the American Republics.
subfiles.summary: Indexes an April 1945 circular placing German- and Japanese-linked firms in American Republics under a Council of Administration.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Circular Telegram on Expropriation Decrees in American Republics
subfiles.to: Chiefs of Missions in the American Republics (except Argentina)

subfiles.about: Memorandum note summarizing an assessment by former Mangyo president Takasaki on the destruction and residual value of Japanese capital in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: May 23 note on Takasaki's finding that only 10% of Japanese industrial investment value in Manchuria survived the war, mostly due to mob looting rather than Soviet removals; he hoped many Japanese personnel would stay to help rebuild.
subfiles.title: Note on Takasaki's Assessment of Japanese Capital and Industry in Manchuria
